clue.text: Water a mare, perhaps, where one's got a bargain

parts.note: a dam is a mother horse, and a mare is one example
a sale is where bargains are got

explanation.surface: Someone takes their mare for a drink, then wonders where they picked up such a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has you watering a horse; in fact 'Water' is the definition and the rest is a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is an old jocular expression for plain drinking water, since Adam had nothing else.

clue.text: Take risks catching old marine creatures

indicators.note: catching means the first phrase's word holds the following letters within it

parts.note: to dice (with death) is to take risks
RM, Royal Marines, gives a marine

explanation.surface: Daredevil divers risk their lives to capture ancient sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marine creatures' looks like one phrase, but 'marine' is RM and only 'creatures' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small rodents, so they are creatures in the broad animal sense.

clue.text: Very little interest reported in fast food?

parts.note: minute means very small

indicators.note: reported signals that a word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a stake is an interest held in something

explanation.surface: A tiny sum of interest is mentioned in a report on fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: A minute steak cooks very quickly, hence the playful 'fast food?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute steak is a thin cut fried in about a minute, so it is literally quick food.

clue.text: Tolerate assistant accepting bribe, at first

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside, so the helper's word holds the letter

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word bribe

explanation.surface: Should one put up with an aide who takes a bribe from the start?
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to put up with it, a synonym of tolerate.

clue.text: Chase what's serious — minor measure being given priority

indicators.note: being given priority means this piece is placed ahead of the other

parts.note: an en is a small printer's measure of width
grave means serious

explanation.surface: A pursuit of something weighty, with a small measure put first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' is the metalworking verb, to decorate by cutting into the surface, not to pursue.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase metal is to engrave or emboss a pattern on it, a craftsman's sense.

clue.text: Disorderly group's endless mirth following joke

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the joke word

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: glee is mirth

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd's laughter keeps on after a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last E of GLEE, leaving GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaggle is a flock of geese, extended to any noisy, unruly bunch of people.

clue.text: Gaunt vagrant outside built-up Indian city, one with huge appetite

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
vagrant means wandering, so the letters of Gaunt are moved about
built-up in a down clue means written from bottom to top

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A thin tramp is found outside a sprawling Indian city, ravenously hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaunt vagrant' looks like a description of the man, but 'vagrant' is the anagram signal and 'built-up' reverses the city in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is Rabelais's giant famed for his enormous appetite.

clue.text: One ruminating, as psychologist turns up out of his head

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the letters read bottom to top
out of his head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss psychologist

explanation.surface: A psychologist appears, having gone out of his mind, chewing things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of his head' drops J from JUNG, leaving UNG; 'turns up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildebeest chews the cud, so it is a ruminant animal, one that ruminates.

clue.text: Accomodation to be extended — dig out central part

indicators.note: central part means the scrambled letters go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: long means extended in length

indicators.note: out signals the letters of dig being rearranged

explanation.surface: Lodgings are to be enlarged by digging out the middle section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DIG into DGI, set in the middle of LONG. The clue's 'Accomodation' is misspelt as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging means a place to stay, rented rooms, so it is accommodation.

clue.text: Quickly deliver jewellery, perhaps best by far

definitions.meaning: read literally: run (deliver quickly) a round of rings

explanation.surface: A courier rushes rings round, outshining all rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is the phrase taken word for word: run a round of rings to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To run rings round someone is an idiom for beating them comprehensively.

clue.text: Tribes plastered in brownish pigment

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, suggesting the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Tribesmen are daubed in brown paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like covering with paint, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a brown pigment made from soot, used for ink washes.

clue.text: Managed a turn, stylish but disorganised

indicators.note: turn means the phrase 'Managed a' is read backwards as a whole

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
chic means stylish

explanation.surface: A smart performer manages a turn, but it is a shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like a noun after 'a', but it is the reversal signal acting on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means without order or control, so chaotic and disorganised.

clue.text: I rejected most tacky uncooked pastry

indicators.note: rejected means the letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: cheesiest means most tacky or tasteless
raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: Someone turns down the tackiest raw pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' takes I out of CHEESIEST, giving CHEESEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese straw is a thin stick of cheesy baked pastry, a savoury snack.

clue.text: Dogged by saucy little sister, 10, coming in

indicators.note: coming in means these letters enter the first word

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky
sis is a short form of sister
ten written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone is followed about by a cheeky little sister aged ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' reads as the verb (followed), but defines as the adjective (determined).
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged means stubbornly determined, which is what persistent means.

clue.text: Some racehorses to draw — one thin round the neck

parts.note: a string is the group of horses kept by one stable or trainer
to tie is to draw, finish level

explanation.surface: Some racehorses are set to dead-heat.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainer's STRING is his stable of racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: A string tie is a very narrow necktie, so a thin one worn at the throat.

clue.text: Nervous, taking part in highly rated gymkhana

indicators.note: taking part in means the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: Riders are tense about competing in a prestigious gymkhana.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymkhana is a horse-riding competition, often for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and anxious, so nervous.

clue.text: Most of material is rather quaint

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tweed is a woollen fabric

explanation.surface: Most of the fabric is somewhat old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final D of TWEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sweet, a British informal word.

clue.text: A dictionary of proper names?

parts.note: a reference book listing notable people, whose entries are names

explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is the annual directory of eminent people, effectively a book of names.

clue.text: Change category of files with scary complexity

indicators.note: complexity suggests the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Folders are moved into new categories because they are frighteningly complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclassify is to assign something to a different class, a different category.

clue.text: Approach shot

definitions.meaning: a photograph or film shot taken from very near

explanation.definitionFit: To close up is to move nearer; a close-up is a camera shot taken at short range.

clue.text: Arguably this lad's loving, and giving a thrill

parts.note: the nursery rhyme says Friday's child is loving and giving, so Friday's, shortened
a lad is a son

explanation.surface: A boy is said to be kind and generous, which gives people a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child...' says 'Friday's child is loving and giving'; this lad is FRI'S SON, 'Arguably' admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement, a thrill.

clue.text: Investigate family in the money? Nothing ensues

indicators.note: ensues means this letter follows after
in means the family word goes inside the money word

parts.note: loot is slang for money
kin is family
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the family is rich and finds there is nothing there.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into something is to examine or investigate it.

clue.text: Lasting impression left by an old boy?

definitions.text: Lasting impression left by an old boy?

parts.words: Lasting impression left by an old boy?
parts.note: a mark in rock left by an ancient creature, while an old boy suggests a fuddy-duddy

explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved imprint of ancient life, and also slang for an old-fashioned person.

clue.text: Finally full, having tucked into square meal

indicators.note: having tucked into means a letter is placed inside the number word

parts.note: four is a square number, two times two

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of full

explanation.surface: Finally full after tucking into a hearty square meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square meal' reads as one phrase, but 'square' gives FOUR and 'meal' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is ground grain, and flour is the finely ground kind.

clue.text: Accept dismissal — those setting exams had to act

parts.note: in cricket a batsman walks, leaving without waiting for the umpire's decision
the boards are the examining bodies that set exams

explanation.surface: Examiners, told they were sacked, had to accept it and put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who knows they are out may WALK off without being given out.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk the boards means to perform on stage, like treading the boards.

clue.text: Item for which someone may pay a fortune

definitions.text: Item for which someone may pay a fortune

parts.words: Item for which someone may pay a fortune
parts.note: an article sold at auction, while a fortune is also one's destiny

explanation.definitionFit: A lot is an item offered at auction, and also a person's fortune in life.

clue.text: Whence the courage to go Dutch?

definitions.text: Whence the courage to go Dutch?

parts.words: Whence the courage to go Dutch?
parts.note: Dutch courage is the bravery that comes from alcohol, poured from a container

explanation.definitionFit: Dutch courage comes from drink, and the container is also slang for nerve.

clue.text: Drink a double, and think hard, having drunk it

indicators.note: having drunk means the first word swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to pore over is to study or think hard
a twin is a double

explanation.surface: Someone orders a double and broods over it after downing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Port wine is a fortified Portuguese wine, a drink.
